summary.core_contribution: The paper redesigns GDB dynamic tracing around LTTng-UST and scalable trace views so multi-threaded CPU/GPU debugging remains usable on heterogeneous many-core systems.
summary.problem: Conventional debugger tracing serializes many threads through shared buffers and stop-the-world flushing, while heterogeneous CPU/GPU execution produces too many threads, waves, and call-stack events for a flat debugger UI.
summary.method: Dynamically insert jump-pad instrumentation from GDB/GDBServer and transfer events through LTTng-UST per-core lock-free-style ring buffers without stopping the target during buffer transfer. Trace Compass aggregates CPU call stacks and provides hierarchical HSA GPU wave/grid views and filters.
summary.findings: The proposed path scales substantially better than default GDB fast tracing on the pbzip2 workload, with much lower growth in tracing overhead as thread count increases. The UI supports focused CPU call-stack and GPU wave-level exploration.
summary.limitations: Instrumentation has instruction-size/location constraints; filters still incur event/context-switch cost; GPU first-level grouping may require manual expansion; closed-source tools were excluded; the evaluation centers on pbzip2 and one GPU setup, with only informal feedback from three engineers rather than a controlled user study.
summary.future_work: No dedicated future-work section is provided. The conclusion identifies a cautious next direction: remove the size limitation by replacing a function frame and instrumenting that frame.
